source_refs.note: Exercise 3.3, Question 14: book p. 89-90, 24 questions (integration by parts); answer key p. 301 (printed under 'Exercise 3.5')

blocks.explanation:
Numerator \(x\cos x - \sin x\) aur denominator \(x^2\) dekh kar quotient rule yaad aata hai: \(\frac{d}{dx}\frac{\sin x}{x} = \frac{x\cos x - \sin x}{x^2}\).
Lekin hum parts se kaam karenge taa ke tareeqa pakka ho.
Integral ko do hisson mein torenge: \(\int \frac{\cos x}{x}\,dx\) aur \(\int \frac{\sin x}{x^2}\,dx\). Dono akele kisi aam function mein nahi nikalte!
Plan: doosre hisse par parts (\(\sin x\) first, \(\frac{1}{x^2}\) second); us mein se \(\int \frac{\cos x}{x}\,dx\) niklega jo pehle hisse ko cancel kar dega.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{x\cos x - \sin x}{x^2}\,dx\), \(x \ne 0\).
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: torenge; \(\int \sin x\cdot x^{-2}\,dx\) par parts, \(\sin x\) first aur \(x^{-2}\) second.

Torein
\[= \int \dfrac{\cos x}{x}\,dx - \int \dfrac{\sin x}{x^2}\,dx\]
Kyun: numerator ke har term ko \(x^2\) se divide kiya: \(\frac{x\cos x}{x^2} = \frac{\cos x}{x}\).

Doosre integral par parts
\[\int \sin x\cdot x^{-2}\,dx = \sin x\left(-\dfrac{1}{x}\right) - \int \left(-\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\cos x\,dx\]
\[= -\dfrac{\sin x}{x} + \int \dfrac{\cos x}{x}\,dx\]
Kyun: \(x^{-2}\) ka integral power rule se \(\frac{x^{-1}}{-1} = -\frac{1}{x}\). Do minus mil kar plus bane. Ab wohi \(\int \frac{\cos x}{x}\,dx\) nikal aaya jo pehle hisse mein hai.

Wapas rakhein: cancel
\[= \int \dfrac{\cos x}{x}\,dx + \dfrac{\sin x}{x} - \int \dfrac{\cos x}{x}\,dx\]
\[= \dfrac{\sin x}{x} + c\]
Kyun: doosre hisse ke aage minus tha, is liye pura bracket ulta ho gaya; dono \(\int \frac{\cos x}{x}\,dx\) cancel.
Dhyan dein: bracket ke aage wala minus dono terms par lagta hai; sirf pehle par laga diya to cancellation nahi hogi.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{\sin x}{x}\right) = \dfrac{x\cos x - \sin x\cdot 1}{x^2}\]
Kyun: quotient rule: (neeche \(\times\) upar ka derivative \(-\) upar \(\times\) neeche ka derivative) / neeche ka square. Bilkul integrand.
